newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products hold firm, but lack of activity.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products hold firm, but lack of activity.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady on Thursday, traders said.

Gasoline was slightly firmer in line with gains in Northwest Europe, although traders said the regions looked fairly balanced. Turkish state oil refinery said it awarded an import tender for 25,000 tonnes of gasoline to Glencore-London at a discount of $16.80 to quotes.

Naphtha was reported to be fairly tight with Far East demand drawing material out of the region once more. Tupras was selling 15,000 tonnes of straight-run material through a tender closing on Friday.
Lacklustre trading interest saw fuel oil prices remain stable despite complaints from some traders that a scarcity of prompt material should boost values.
Large flows of high sulphur material to Asia, Cuba and Romania have soaked up excess stock and the arbitrage to the Far East was beginning to close, traders said.

"What has been done is going and people are looking at April now," said one player. Buyers complained prices were being driven by nothing more than paper trade, which eased in value in the late afternoon.
Those holders of Russian cargoes large enough to be worked eastwards were the envy of the gas oil market in the Med where local demand continues to be poor.
Russian cargoes were seen as very hard to get hold of with nearly all scheduled cargoes already with Asian homes.
Dealers said a prime arb cargo could attract around fob high quotes +$4. Italian spec gas oil was looking for fob high quotes +$3.
